subject: No-learn evidence and output-licensing request
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Harry Lawson <harry.lawson@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: no-train commitment, ops evidence, and output licensing

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited about the latency/cost profile. Before we proceed with a POC we need to close a couple of privacy/contract items related to patient-facing prompts. Specifically: 

1) No-learning / no-training commitment: We require a clear written commitment that tenant inputs (including prompts and any PII) will not be used to improve Redwood models or model weights. If that is not feasible, we need a narrow definition of what "no-train" covers and a technical proof-of-process.

2) Evidence packet for controls: We need artifacts showing operational controls for our tenant and region (US). Example items: KV/prefix cache eviction policy, retention windows, sample audit log export (redacted), subprocessor inventory for the services touching inference, and the ops playbook for incident-level data leakage.

3) Output / derivative licensing: We need to confirm that model outputs generated from our prompts are owned by Nimbus (or at least licensed for unlimited internal use) and that Redwood will not assert derivative rights. A proposed clause or amendment would speed review.

Can you (or your privacy team) provide an evidence packet and proposed amendment language we can give to our GC? We attached our DPA draft for reference (see Nimbus_DPA_draft.docx).

Appreciate a quick read — we're aiming to start a limited POC the week of Sep 20, so a response in the next 4 business days would be ideal.

Best,
Emma

Subject: Fwd: Request: no-train commitment, ops evidence, and output licensing — action items

Folks — forwarding Nimbus' ask. They want: (1) a tenant-level no-train commitment, (2) an evidence packet with ops artifacts, and (3) a short amendment on output/derivative licensing. POC target is week of Sep 20.

Below is my proposed amendment language — feel free to edit and add technical footnotes: 

"Proposed amendment (draft):
1. No-Training Commitment: Redwood agrees not to use Customer Data (including prompts, user inputs, or model outputs that contain Customer Data) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any of Redwood’s proprietary models or model weights. This commitment applies to data collected from the Redwood-hosted inference service for the Customer's tenant(s) identified in the Agreement, for the duration of the Agreement and for a period of 12 months following termination unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing.

2. Output Rights: Redwood acknowledges that outputs generated in response to Customer Data are the Customer’s Confidential Information. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, and create derivative works of such outputs for internal business purposes. Redwood will not assert ownership or derivative rights over outputs derived from Customer Data.

3. Evidence Packet: Redwood will provide a redacted ops evidence packet that includes: subprocessor inventory for services touching inference; a sample redacted audit log export (TLS- and IP-redacted); description of KV cache retention and eviction policies; and the operational runbook for data handling and incident response. Some items will be redacted for security reasons; Redwood will provide attestation where full disclosure is not possible.

-- End proposed amendment --

Jonas: can you confirm what we can commit to in section 1 (length of post-termination protection, whether aggregated telemetry counts as training, etc.) and produce the evidence pack items we can share? 
Monica: please validate the subprocessor list and indicate if any of Nimbus' requests require a separate NDA or a CSAT.

I propose we get a first draft and evidence pack together Monday afternoon and send to Emma for GC review.

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: no-train commitment, ops evidence, and output licensing — action items

Thanks Rachel — quick status and attachments (see ops_evidence_packet_v1.zip).

What we can commit to today: 
- No-training: We can provide a tenant-scoped no-train commitment that excludes aggregated telemetry that is irreversibly anonymized and cannot be traced back to individual inputs. We will not use tenant-identifiable inputs (raw prompts, PII) to update proprietary model weights.
- Post-termination period: 12 months is acceptable; if Nimbus needs a longer tail we can propose a commercial add-on.
- Aggregated telemetry: telemetry that is aggregated at scale and where PII has been removed with documented techniques (hashing+salted truncation, k-anonymity checks) is not considered training for the purposes of the commitment. This is because those signals are used only for performance monitoring and capacity planning, not model updates. If Nimbus requires complete prohibition of telemetry-derived signals for model improvement, that's a negotiable restriction and may impact unit economics.

Attachments included for review (redacted where necessary):
- ops_evidence_packet_v1.zip (contains: subprocessor_inventory.csv, sample_audit_log_redacted.csv, kv_cache_policy.pdf, retention_table.csv, incident_runbook_excerpt.pdf)
- redwood_no-train_amendment_v1.docx (tracked changes in update)

Open items for Rachel/Legal to resolve before sending to Nimbus GC: 
1) Whether "irreversibly anonymized" meets Nimbus' legal standard — we should include a short appendix describing the anonymization steps and a statement of technical measures.
2) Confirm that the sample audit log can be redacted to the level Nimbus expects (we removed client identifiers and IPs).
3) Confirm whether Nimbus needs a SOC2 + bridging letter or an attestation signed by our CISO.

Proposed timeline: final amendment + evidence pack to Emma by COB Mon Sep 6. If they want DocuSign we can route it same day.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Emma — quick clarifying note before we send the formal pack: Redwood maintains a policy and technical separation between telemetry pipelines used for monitoring/capacity and any model training pipelines. Aggregated telemetry for capacity, anomaly detection, and performance monitoring is stored in a separate analytics cluster and is not used to fine-tune, re-train, or update model weights for any proprietary or open-source variants that could be later served to customers.

Jonas will include a short appendix describing the telemetry separation and the anonymization steps we take. We'll include the amendment doc and the evidence packet by COB today.

Thanks,
Rachel
